title: When Hammers star Brandon Scanlin told his mom he's coming home to play AHL hockey 'she almost started crying'
description: After years without professional hockey in Hamilton, the wait is almost over. The Hamilton Hammers will play their first regular-season home game Friday night, hosting the Toronto Marlies at TD Coliseum as the new AHL team begins its inaugural season.
text:
After years without professional hockey in Hamilton, the wait is almost over the Hamilton Hammers will play their first regular-season home game Friday night, hosting the Toronto Marlies at TD Coliseum as the new AHL team begins its inaugural season. After years without professional hockey in Hamilton, the wait is almost over the Hamilton Hammers will play their first regular-season home game Friday night, hosting the Toronto Marlies at TD Coliseum in its inaugural season. The 26-year-old defenceman grew up on Hamilton's West Mountain, attended Westmount Secondary School and played minor hockey in the city.

"It's a very exciting moment," Scanlin said. I love the people in this city, and to be able to represent the city is something that's pretty special to me." Scanlin said his family was thrilled when he told them he was coming home. Brandon Scanlin says he will have friends and family at the home opener on Friday. (Vince Neil Media) Friday's game will give the people who have supported him throughout his career a chance to finally see him play professionally in his hometown, he said.
